title: Autonomous SLO actuation for model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an autonomous SLO-actuation layer that can trigger partial or full rollbacks for model rollouts (canary, A/B, and shadow) based on multi-dimensional SLO violations: p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost per request, and throughput. The feature must support per-route and per-customer baselines, incorporate statistical confidence, and allow progressive rollback/doze-down strategies rather than binary kill switches. Provide operator-visible explanations for each actuation and tight integration with the Console rollout UI and existing alerting/incident workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Service can detect SLO regressions on a canary at 95% confidence within the configured evaluation window (default 5 minutes) for any combination of latency/error/cost/throughput
Operator can choose among actuation policies: immediate full rollback, graded percentage rollback (e.g., reduce canary to 10% -> 0%), or automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant
All actuations are logged with reason, metric windows, statistical test name, effect size, and supporting query links visible in Console
Automated triggers respect per-customer overrides and minimum traffic thresholds to avoid spurious rollbacks on small samples
Post-decision pipeline creates a revert PR or automated plan (for Dedicated/Private) with telemetry snapshot and suggested remediation steps
implementation_notes: Core detection primitives: implement Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) for error-rate shifts, and EWMA or ADWIN for latency drift detection. Use bootstrap or permutation tests for token-cost regressions where distribution is heavy-tailed.
Run detection independently per route/model-variant and then compose signals using weighted voting (weight by traffic fraction and business criticality).
Design an extensible policy language with predicates (metric, comparator, duration, confidence) and actions (scale down percentage, rollback variant, route to fallback, notify-on-call).
Integrate with prefix/KV cache indicators to distinguish cache-warmup anomalies from model regressions (cache_traces in telemetry).
Expose dry-run mode where triggers are evaluated but not acted upon; results should be visible in Console and in a dedicated audit log table.
implementation_todos: P0: Define canonical metric names and units for all SLOs and add to observability schema
P0: Add SPRT and EWMA detectors to runtime metrics service; unit tests + synthetic workload harness
P1: Policy language parser and storage (small CRD-like schema backed by control plane DB)
P1: Console UI components for policy authoring and per-rollout explanation cards
P2: Wire actions to rollout controller and Dedicated/Private deployment agents
P2: End-to-end e2e tests using shadow traffic + fault injection scenarios
testing_plan: Synthetic traffic generator that can inject latency tails, error bursts, and token-cost regressions per-route; must support gradual and sudden perturbations
Run A/B experiments in staging with known regressions to validate detection time and false positive rate (target FPR < 1% at production traffic volumes)
Power analysis: determine minimum sample sizes for each metric to achieve 90/95% detection power for realistic effect sizes (e.g., 20% latency increase at p95)
Chaos scenarios: introduce transient infra blips, network partitions, and slow KV cache to validate detectors don’t misclassify infrastructural incidents as model regressions
Playback recorded customer production traces against simulated rolled-out model variants to verify action correctness
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable detectors in dry-run for top 10 internal routes for 2 weeks; iterate on thresholds and alerts
Phase 2 (canary beta): enable automatic graded-actuation for 5% canaries on internal customers; require manual approval for full rollback
Phase 3 (public opt-in): expose policy controls in Console for opt-in early-adopter customers with safelist
Phase 4 (default-on): enable for all hosted endpoints with conservative defaults and ability to opt-out via project-level policy
Fallback path: any auto-actuation triggers a PagerDuty alert and creates an incident with telemetry snapshot and rollback artifact
rollback_triggers: Latency: sustained p95 increase > 30% relative to baseline over evaluation window and EWMA change score > threshold
Error rate: absolute error-rate exceeds 0.5% for high-traffic routes or 2x baseline with SPRT reaching rejection boundary
Token cost: median cost-per-request increases by > 15% with statistically significant shift (bootstrap p < 0.05)
Throughput: throughput drop causing SLA breach (backpressure cascades) for two consecutive evaluation windows
Composite: weighted alarm when two of the above metrics show medium severity within same window (configurable weights)
Minimum traffic floor: no automatic rollback unless route has processed >= configured sample_count (default 500 requests) in the window
monitoring_queries: Latency p95: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) FROM tokens WHERE route = 'X' AND variant = 'canary' AND time > now() - 5m
Error rate SPRT: CALL sprt_test('errors', 'baseline_errors', alpha=0.05, beta=0.2, N1=baseline_N, N2=canary_N)
Token cost delta: SELECT mean(cost_usd_per_request) FROM requests WHERE variant IN ('baseline','canary') GROUP BY variant
Throughput: SELECT rate(count(*), 1m) FROM requests WHERE variant = 'canary'
